title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN hero used as Sultan Mehmed II: Saladin died in 1193, was a Kurdish Ayyubid, not an Ottoman, and is 260 years out of period. The engine offers other options (a generic Champion/Cavalier renamed, or the Turkish Janissary line) so this named-hero mismatch was avoidable.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x6 as the vegetation around Constantinople: Thrace and the Bosphorus are oak/pine country, not palm; the engine has abundant temperate forest tiles.

CAMEL_RIDER x4 in the Ottoman siege line: the 1453 besieging army was built around janissary infantry, azaps, sipahi horse and the great bombard; camels were baggage animals, not a shock arm. HAND_CANNONEER/JANISSARY was available in the engine and unused.

No Wonder placed for Hagia Sophia — the Byzantine Wonder in the engine literally IS Hagia Sophia, yet the church is apparently represented by a plain MONASTERY, undercutting the scenario's own central objective.

issues_found: Player 2's commander is the SALADIN hero — a Kurdish sultan who died in 1193 — standing in for Mehmed II, some 260 years out of period; the engine ships no Mehmed hero, so a renamed generic Champion/Cavalier or Turkish elite unit was the correct choice and this substitution was entirely avoidable

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the defenders may not render as Byzantines nor the besiegers as Turks; architecture set, unit roster flavour and the iconic Byzantine/Turkish tech are all left to chance

Ottoman force includes 4 CAMEL_RIDER — desert cavalry inappropriate for the 1453 Thracian siege lines and not a Turkish unit in the engine; sipahi cavalry are better served by the Cavalier/Knight already present

No water tiles or ships anywhere on the map, yet Wave 3 narrates Mehmed's fleet being dragged overland into the Golden Horn and the objectives demand guarding the sea walls; the naval flanking threat is pure text with nothing placed
TREE_PALM_FOREST as the map's only woodland is wrong for the Thracian/Bosphorus environment

Victory is coded as DESTROY_OBJECT on the enemy leader — the defenders sallying out to kill the Sultan is the opposite of the historical situation, in which Mehmed survived and the garrison could only try to outlast the assaults; a timer-survival victory was the correct encoding
The victory narration ('Constantinople stands - the walls of Rome hold once more!') asserts a counterfactual outcome as the reward state, teaching the player that the City held
Hagia Sophia is represented by an ordinary MONASTERY with no distinguishing marker; a Wonder or a walled precinct would have read as the great church
Only 8 villagers and no stone-repair economy support the repeatedly stated 'repair the breaches' mechanic; the Wall Breached trigger merely CREATE_OBJECTs rather than enabling meaningful repair

SALADIN is placed as the Ottoman commander for Mehmed II — a Kurdish Ayyubid sultan of the 1180s standing in for an Ottoman sultan of 1453, an avoidable cross-culture and cross-era error when a renamed generic unit (or a Janissary/Champion named 'Mehmed II') was available

Both players' civilizations are left RANDOM, so architecture sets and unit bonuses may render Byzantines and Ottomans as, e.g., Celts and Vikings; the engine ships both Byzantines and Turks and neither was assigned

The Ottoman assault force uses CHAMPION x6 and CAMEL_RIDER x4 rather than the Turkish Janissary the engine actually ships — janissaries were the signature assault troops of the 1453 storm, and camel riders were not part of the army before Constantinople

The Golden Horn sea-wall theme is narrated ('Mehmed's fleet, dragged overland past Galata... now floats upon the Golden Horn') but there is no water, no dock, and not a single ship placed anywhere on the 120x120 map; Wave 3 is delivered by the same land patrol as the other waves
TREE_PALM_FOREST x6 as the map's only vegetation is wrong for Thrace and the Bosphorus

Only ONAGER x1 and SCORPION x2 plus a Siege Workshop for the defenders, and no Byzantine-specific defensive flavour (e.g., Sea Walls/Harbour, cataphract-type troops); STONE_WALL x124 with GUARD_TOWER x5 and a single KEEP is a thin abstraction of the triple Theodosian line — the inner/outer wall and moat structure is not represented

Victory fires on the death of the enemy commander, producing the counterfactual 'the Ottoman host breaks and flees. Constantinople stands' — the City fell on 29 May 1453 and Mehmed II survived to reign for 28 more years

Hagia Sophia is represented by a MONASTERY that must be destroyed for defeat, but historically Hagia Sophia was never destroyed — it was converted, and the City's fall turned on the breach at the Gate of St. Romanus, not on the church burning
